problem:
$$
∃{x}_{\begin{aligned} \\ ↑ \\ \text{I}\end{aligned}}\in R,\,2-{x}_{\begin{aligned} \\ ↑ \\ \text{II}\end{aligned}}={w}_{\begin{aligned} \\ ↑ \\ \text{III}\end{aligned}}
$$

Which occurrences of the variables in the expression above are free?
worked_solution:
Let's examine our expression and mark the occurrences of the variables as bound $(\text{b})$ or free $(\text{f}).$

- Occurrence I of the variable $x$ is *bound* since it's placed right next to the quantifier $∃:$

$$
∃\,{x}_{\begin{aligned} \\ ↑ \\ \text{b}\end{aligned}}\in R,\,2-x=w
$$

- Occurrence II of the variable $x$ is *bound* since it lies within the scope of the quantifier $∃x$ that uses $x:$

$$
∃\,x\in R,\,\overset{\text{scope of }∃x}{\overset{⏞}{2-{x}_{\begin{aligned} \\ ↑ \\ \text{b}\end{aligned}}=w}}
$$

- Occurrence III of the variable $w$ is *free* since it isn't placed right next to a quantifier and it doesn't lie within the scope of a quantifier that uses $w.$

The occurrences of variables in the expression are as follows:

$$
∃{x}_{\begin{aligned} \\ ↑ \\ \text{b}\end{aligned}}\in R,\,2-{x}_{\begin{aligned} \\ ↑ \\ \text{b}\end{aligned}}={w}_{\begin{aligned} \\ ↑ \\ \text{f}\end{aligned}}
$$

Therefore, the free occurrence is "III only."
